key_insight: A 3D thermomechanical model of AA2024 aluminum–Cu-DHP copper radial friction welding predicted asymmetric heating, with a peak interface temperature of 750 °C and localized deformation.
engineering_relevance: The model helps interpret heat distribution and material flow in dissimilar aluminum–copper radial friction welds.
method: Coupled 3D finite element modelling in ANSYS Workbench 2023 R1 at 1,400 rpm and 30 MPa.
Optical metallography and Vickers microhardness testing.
Comparison with thermocouple measurements and aluminum-side thermomechanically affected zone width.
evidence_signal: Thermocouple and zone-width comparisons supported directly comparable model predictions; approximately 157 HV in the affected zone provided complementary evidence of localized hardening.
watch_item: Friction and radiation assumptions, omitted latent heat, and absent microstructural kinetics limit interpretation; hardness does not directly measure strain or identify phases.
paper_title: Three-Dimensional Thermomechanical Analysis of Radial Friction Welding of Dissimilar Copper-Aluminum Alloys: Finite Element Modelling and Experimental Validation
